sections.h2: How does probate work in Pennsylvania?
sections.html:
Probate in Pennsylvania runs through the Register of Wills in the county where the decedent had a last family or principal residence. That office grants letters, which are the court-recognized proof that one person may act for the estate. Disputes and sale approvals go to the orphans' court division of the same county.

For a house, letters are the first gate. Without them, nobody can sign a deed for the estate, and a title company will not insure a buyer. The rules sit in Title 20 of the Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes, which is the Probate, Estates and Fiduciaries Code. This page follows that title from the petition through the sale of the house and the distribution of proceeds.

sections.h2: Which county's Register of Wills handles the estate?
sections.html:
Section 3151 says letters for a Pennsylvania domiciliary are granted only by the register of the county where the decedent had a last family or principal residence. A decedent who lived in Erie County and owned a second house elsewhere is still probated in Erie County. If the decedent was domiciled outside Pennsylvania, any county where estate property sits may grant the letters, and those letters are then exclusive across the Commonwealth.

The petition must be sworn. Section 3153 requires the decedent's name, age, domicile, last residence and date and place of death, the heirs where there is no will, and the estimated value of personal property plus the estimated value and location of real property in Pennsylvania. Expect the house address to appear on the petition itself.

sections.h2: Who gets letters, and in what order?
sections.html:
If the will names an executor, section 3155(a) directs the register to grant letters testamentary to that person, even if the executor has declined a trust under the will. With no will, or no executor who acts, letters of administration go to a person in a priority list.

Priority for letters of administration under 20 Pa.C.S. 3155(b)
OrderPerson
1Those entitled to the residuary estate under the will
2The surviving spouse
3Intestate heirs, with preference by size of share
4Principal creditors of the decedent
5Other fit persons

A person who renounces may name a nominee, in the register's discretion. Section 3155(c) adds a waiting period: letters for creditors and other fit persons cannot issue until 30 days after death unless the higher-ranking persons consent.

sections.h2: Can a house skip probate through the small estate process?
sections.html:
Usually not, because the small estate petition in section 3102 excludes real estate from the $50,000 figure. The court may direct distribution of personal property up to $50,000 in gross value, and the court's authority is not restricted because the decedent owned real estate. But that process distributes personal property. A house still needs a person with authority to convey it.

Section 3101 gives other shortcuts that never reach real estate. An employer may pay up to $10,000 in wages or benefits to a spouse, child, parent, sibling in that order of preference, whether or not a representative has been appointed. Neither shortcut replaces letters when the house must be sold.

sections.h2: What can the personal representative do with the real estate?
sections.html:
The representative has the right to take possession of, maintain and administer the decedent's real and personal estate, with one exception: real estate occupied at death by an heir or devisee with the decedent's consent. Under section 3311, the representative collects rents and income until the property is sold or distributed, and makes reasonable expenditures to preserve it. The same section says nothing limits the power to sell real estate occupied by an heir or devisee.

For sale, the powers in section 3351 are broad. Unless the will says otherwise, the representative may sell at public or private sale any real property not specifically devised, and may sell specifically devised property with the devisee's joinder. If the will withholds the power, or a judicial sale effect is advisable, section 3353 requires an order of the orphans' court division. Section 3357 then passes the decedent's full title to the buyer, discharged from legacy liens and estate debts, provided any required bond was given.

  • No will power to sell: ask the court for a section 3353 order.
  • House specifically left to one person: that person joins the deed.
  • Heir living in the house: the representative can still sell it.

sections.h2: What happens to a vacant or burdened house during probate?
sections.html:
The representative carries the duty to maintain the house, because section 3311 makes preservation of estate property part of the job. The statute calls for reasonable expenditures necessary to preserve it. Heirs who live far away often find the first months of probate expensive for exactly this reason.

Section 3312 gives one pressure valve. When property is of no value to the estate, the court may authorize the representative to renounce the right to administer it. A house with debts above its worth can fall into that category, though the court decides, and an attorney should advise before anyone asks.

Real estate taxes also continue. Under 53 Pa.C.S. 8863, property of a decedent's estate may be assessed in the name of the decedent or the personal representative, so tax bills may still arrive in the decedent's name. Ask the county assessment office to update the mailing address once letters issue.

sections.h2: What must be advertised, filed and paid before distributing sale proceeds?
sections.html:
The representative must advertise the grant of letters in one newspaper of general circulation near the decedent's residence and in the legal periodical designated by court rule, once a week for three successive weeks. Section 3162 requires the notice to invite claims and ask debtors to pay. This advertisement starts a clock in section 3532: a representative who distributes at their own risk, without an audit, is free of liability to a claimant unless the claim became known within one year after the first complete advertisement, or later but before distribution.

The inventory is due under section 3301(c) by the date the account is filed or the inheritance tax return is due, whichever is earlier, and any party in interest may demand an earlier filing. Inheritance tax is delinquent nine months after death, with a 5 percent discount if paid within three months, per the Department of Revenue.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale fit into probate?
sections.html:
A cash sale can close as soon as letters exist and the title company is satisfied with the signing authority. The estate avoids months of repairs, staging and listing, and stops paying carrying costs on an empty house. The representative still handles the inheritance tax, advertisement and accounting.

Bring the letters, the will if there is one, the death certificate and any court order to the title company, and ask which documents it requires from the Register of Wills. If an heir lives in the house, plan a move-out date in writing before the closing.

faqs.q: Do I need probate to sell a house in Pennsylvania?
faqs.a: Yes, in most cases. The small estate process covers personal property only, so a house needs a personal representative holding letters from the Register of Wills.

faqs.q: Which county do I file in?
faqs.a: File in the county where the decedent had a last family or principal residence. Section 3151 says letters for a Pennsylvania domiciliary are granted only by that county's register.

faqs.q: Can an heir living in the house be forced out for the sale?
faqs.a: The representative's power to sell is not limited because an heir or devisee lives there. How to end the occupancy is a question for the orphans' court or an attorney, and a written move-out date helps.

faqs.q: How long are creditors given to make a claim?
faqs.a: A representative who distributes at their own risk is protected against claims unknown within one year after the first complete advertisement of letters, or later but before distribution. The advertisement runs once a week for three weeks.

faqs.q: What happens if there is no will and no relatives?
faqs.a: Under a change effective January 16, 2026, the estate goes first to an endowed community fund in the decedent's municipality, then school district, then county, and only then to the Commonwealth.
